A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DyME by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. V1 ends with references; v2 adds readable supplementary Sections S1–S3. Shared material can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original SVLM training and evaluation across medical VQA, chart understanding and geometry, including performance comparisons, training curves and component ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds controlled training comparisons, additional benchmarks, efficiency measurements and human evaluation of reasoning traces.

M1.justification: The binary SFT/GRPO switch and core losses remain. V2 adds an explicit Pure DyME variant using static supervision and a conventional trace reward, and expands the visual checker from visual-fact recall to include stylistic and structural alignment. V1 already allowed templates to adapt through exploration, so the dynamic example-pool description is largely additional detail.

E1.justification: V2 adds A-OKVQA for complex-scene/world-knowledge reasoning and GSM8K for text-only mathematical reasoning (Table S6), substantially extending v1's exclusively visual, three-domain coverage. SLAKE, ChartQA and Geo170K-to-MathVerse evaluation are retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds separately reported Two-stage variants with and without KL, reward-threshold switching, cosine SFT annealing and hard-mining SFT budgets (Table 1). Figure S2 also compares CHORD and LUFFY through off-policy influence trajectories, rather than accuracy. These substantially broaden the training-strategy comparisons. LLaVA-1.5's geometry comparison disappears from Table 2.

E3.justification: New protocols include controlled Low/Medium/High CoT supervision, switching-threshold and training-budget comparisons, epoch-based baseline selection, larger base/helper-model configurations, timing measurements and human assessment of 100 randomly sampled ChartQA cases. Original domain splits and sample counts are retained in Table S1. Fact acquisition is now described as automated, although the geometry source remains underspecified as 'Collected'.

E4.justification: V1's component ablation and training curves are retained. V2 adds analyses of supervision quality, switching rules, visual-fact supervision, output templates, training duration, helper size and off-policy influence, plus human evaluation of CoT validity (Tables 1, 4, S2–S5 and S7; Figure S2). Qualitative cases expand, although Figure S4 contains internally inconsistent traces.

E5.justification: V2 newly mentions repeated Two-stage trials and states that DyME achieves its tuning-comparison result in a single training run without epoch selection (S2.2). This is limited run-information disclosure, not evidence of increased repetitions. Neither version reports seed identities, repeated-run dispersion, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The main DyME averages of 55.6, 55.4 and 58.1 and the component-ablation accuracies remain unchanged. V2 adds extensive results, including A-OKVQA 73.0 versus Two-stage 54.2 and GSM8K 55.3 versus GRPO 49.5 (Table S6). Table 2 removes LLaVA-1.5's geometry score of 6.7 and average of 31.3. These are additions and removals, not improvements over matched v1 scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the SFT/GRPO objectives, gradient comparison, binary switching rule and combined loss. V2 restates the unit-advantage interpretation more briefly but supplies no substantive new derivation, theorem or proof. The appendix primarily adds implementation information and empirical analyses.

C1.justification: The central claims of enabling SVLM thinking through dynamic SFT/RL switching and achieving cross-domain gains remain. V2 explicitly claims that switching alone provides a standalone stabilizing strategy, presents visual supervision as complementary, and qualifies the abstract's benefits around specialized tasks. This refines contribution attribution and applicability.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive discussion of computation versus annotation cost, helper-model capacity, structured templates and visual supervision as a denoising mechanism. It identifies limits involving abstract semantics, memes and dense scenes, suggesting Pure DyME as an alternative. It also corrects v1's reversed prose attribution of the memorization and exploration ablation drops to agree with Table 3.

D1.justification: V2 supplies visual-fact extraction, refiner and checker prompts, describes the dynamic example pool, and provides supervision-quality and complete training-data examples (S1 and S3). Table 4 adds runtime measurements and the new timing experiment's eight-H800 hardware context. These materially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's brief descriptions; the code-access URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds a dedicated hybrid-training discussion and positions DyME against CHORD's annealing and LUFFY's off-policy shaping, developed further in S2.2 and Figure S2. This substantially expands the closest-method comparison beyond v1's focus on separate SFT/RL paradigms and two-stage training, alongside additional citations supporting the expanded coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Experiments are reorganized into algorithmic validation and full-system effectiveness, followed by efficiency and applicability discussion. Setup information moves into the new supplement. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond the added experiments themselves.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 3 are redrawn; new main-text validation and efficiency tables and numerous supplementary tables and figures are added. V1's setup Table 1 becomes Table S1, Table 3 is relocated and compressed, and Table 2 loses its parameter-count column. The conference template also changes typography, headers and page composition.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves the evidence separating switching benefits from supervision quality through controlled Pure DyME experiments, stronger baseline checks and human evaluation of reasoning traces. Detailed prompts address v1's underdocumented visual supervision, while cost and applicability discussions make the claims easier to assess. Some new Figure S4 examples contain contradictory reasoning, and uncertainty estimates remain absent, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and transparency.
